# M11 novelty control adjudication

On 25 September 2026, a fresh-context model reviewer compared the three paired public-source abstracts without seeing the fixture's provisional overlap labels. This is an independent **abstract-level model assessment**, not a blinded human domain review, full-text review, or expert validation. The papers were identified by PMID before adjudication; each conclusion is pairwise and says nothing about novelty relative to all literature.

| Pair | Primary-source abstracts | Related prior-art overlap | Same scientific idea? | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| STMN2 / UNC13A | [30643298](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30643298/) and [42596024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42596024/) | Yes | No | Both concern cryptic RNA processing associated with TDP-43, but the first addresses STMN2 premature polyadenylation and motor-neuron axonal regeneration, while the second addresses an UNC13A cryptic-exon variant and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease. The latter reports no association of the variant with TDP-43 pathology. |
| SARS-CoV-2 entry / endothelial inflammation | [32142651](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32142651/) and [42150851](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42150851/) | Shared topic only | No | ACE2/TMPRSS2-dependent viral entry and spike S1/interferon/ISG15-dependent endothelial inflammation differ in mechanism, setting, and outcome. TMPRSS2 dependence is cell-contextual in the entry paper. |
| Qa-1 tumor checkpoint / MCMV response | [36151395](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36151395/) and [41417899](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41417899/) | Yes | No | The tumor study concerns Qa-1 inhibiting CD8 cells through NKG2A/CD94 in checkpoint-treated cancer models. The MCMV study concerns Qa-1 presenting viral peptide to protective CD8 cells. The first abstract does not itself establish the fixture's “mouse” detail. |

Each cited paper supports the central mechanism of its corresponding fixture draft at the abstract level, subject to the qualifiers above. The original single-curator labels remain in [`novelty-result-conditioned-fixture-v1.json`](novelty-result-conditioned-fixture-v1.json); this second assessment agrees on pairwise non-duplication but does not establish search performance or expert-level label validity. The later maintained PubMed comparison returned three IDs for each positive search but retrieved **none** of the three target PMIDs in its top three. The result file contains only IDs; [`novelty-current-results-metadata-v1.json`](novelty-current-results-metadata-v1.json) now retains the 18 corresponding public title/DOI records from that run's local keyless cache, without making another request. Several titles are plainly off-topic, including cardiac MRI and cyanophage engineering for a Qa-1 tumor query. The maintained tool sorts by publication date and its final search rung ORs all terms, which can explain off-topic recent papers; the probe did not capture which rung produced each result, so this is a code-supported explanation rather than observed wire provenance. M11-NOV-01a therefore remains open until a current-path result-conditioned fixture and its retrieval/error protocol are frozen.
